I will keep the farm simple and steady because I am 59, I farm mostly by myself, and I have only 20 mu. My main land will stay in the wheat-maize rotation because that is what fits my experience, my irrigation condition, and my habit of managing risk. I will put 16 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land, and I will keep 4 mu in cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen for a stable stand, add moderate phosphorus and potassium, irrigate at the key times, and use rotary tillage because it is practical for me. After wheat harvest, I will plant hybrid maize on that same 16 mu and keep tillage light with no-tillage so I save labor and do not lose time. For cotton, I will keep a smaller area because it takes more work, but I will still plant it for diversification and cash income. I will not chase the highest input level; I will aim for a crop plan I can actually manage well with one person and well water.
